title: Delete Node in a BST
summary: Remove key from the BST if it exists, then return a root of a valid BST with exactly the remaining values.

contractDetails.constraints: 0–10000 nodes with distinct values in [−100000,100000]. key is in the same range. Input and result use level-order values with null for missing children.
contractDetails.output-checking: Serialize the returned root with null child positions. Verify strict BST ordering and the original value set minus key. Accept alternative valid shapes. No original-node identity constraint is imposed.

statement: Remove key from the BST if it exists, then return a root of a valid BST with exactly the remaining values. A missing key leaves the value set unchanged. Different valid output shapes are allowed.

examples.explanation: Replacing the deleted root with its successor gives one valid result.

constraints: 0–10000 nodes with distinct values in [−100000,100000]. key is in the same range. Input and result use level-order values with null for missing children.
hints: Conceptual: Deleting a node must keep every remaining value on the correct side of its ancestors.
Directional: Handle zero, one, and two children separately.
Implementation: For two children, replace the value with its next value in sorted order, then remove that successor from the right subtree.
complexityAnalysis: O(h) time and O(1) auxiliary solution space for iterative deletion.
